summary: WebSocket stream terminates after ~60s during long multi-part responses on Dedicated pool
description: Issue summary: ParcelFlow reports that WebSocket streams for long chat responses consistently terminate after approximately 55–70 seconds into a response. This started after a rollout on 2026-03-10. Impact: Multiple users see truncated replies mid-generation causing failed UX and token re-requests. Affects a small subset of long-response use cases on the customer's dedicated GPU pool. Environment: prod-us-east, customer Dedicated pool (pool-id: ded-pool-74), requests use WebSocket transport with keepalive pings enabled by client. Observed behavior: Stream connection drops with TCP FIN from load balancer and client sees "connection closed" without an explicit 5xx. Expected behavior: Long-running generation streams should stay open until generation completes (several minutes for >2k-token outputs).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use ParcelFlow account on dedicated pool ded-pool-74
2) Open WebSocket to /v1/chat/stream endpoint (w/ Authorization header)
3) Send a prompt that yields long multi-part response (>= 1500 tokens) using redwood-xlarge-7B with streaming enabled
4) Observe disconnect consistently at ~60 seconds into generation (repro rate ~85% for long outputs)
logs: proxy-trace: downstream FIN observed -> upstream half-close not propagated; worker still generating
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: NLB idle timeout (60s) closing the connection when traffic pattern has quiet periods between token flushes.
Checked proxy metrics: streaming-proxy shows correct keepalive forwarding for HTTP/1.1 chunk flushes but NLB reports idle-termination around 60s for these connections.
Observed that adaptive-batching-v2 introduced an extra internal buffer step that delays the first token flush for very long-context workloads, creating a quiet window longer than NLB timeout.
Ded-pool worker logs show generation continues after downstream FIN, but SDK/client sees closed socket causing retry logic and duplicate prompt submissions.
No 5xx from serving-runtime; kernel preemption spikes were low. GPU worker remained allocated and reported steady throughput.
Related: SUP-332110 notes a websocket fragmentation hang in a different customer environment; cross-referenced for proxy tracing patterns.
resolution: Mitigation deployed 2026-03-12 16:20Z: increased NLB idle timeout from 60s -> 300s for ded-pool-74 load balancer (config change: infra/prod/nlb/ded-pool-74.yml #PR 667)
Temporary rollback: disabled adaptive-batching-v2 for ParcelFlow routing rule (feature-flag: adaptive-batching-v2=off for customer id cf-4091)
Observed after mitigation: repro rate dropped to ~5% for same prompts. Customer confirmed major UX flows functional.

Follow-up actions: hardening task assigned to SRE/Runtime teams to ensure token-flush heartbeat is guaranteed within 30s (INT task created), and review default NLB timeout assumptions for dedicated pools. See linked PRs and runbook updates.
Status: mitigated; root cause analysis in progress and assigned to Eng (runtime + infra) for permanent fix.
